title: Find out why the whole test run hangs in the Mac's picture and text reading work
goal: On 2026-10-10 the full test run stopped making progress twice, stuck inside the Mac's own HEIF picture writing, text recognition and sound reading, while the same tests pass on their own. Until it is understood, a runner cannot get a single green run before committing.
notes: Seen by runner on a-spinner-can-turn-about-the-middle-of-the-artbo, 03:10-03:50. `Scripts/test.sh` twice sat at 0% CPU for 9-19 min (swiftpm-testing-helper). `sample <pid>` showed threads parked in CGImageDestinationFinalize > HEIFWritePlugin > CMPhoto > VCPHEVC (PackageIOTests, ImageCodecTests), VNRecognizeTextRequest (ReadPageWeightFixtureTests, ReadRunAsTextFixtureTests, ARefusedReadIsToldApartTests via TextReader) and AVAssetReader (SoundFile.peaks). `swift test --skip-build --filter ImageCodecTests` alone: 6 pass in 0.05s. Split run passed: `Scripts/test.sh --skip 'PhotonzRenderTests|PhotonzMediaTests'` 11003 pass in 42s; `swift test --skip-build --filter 'PhotonzRenderTests|PhotonzMediaTests'` 1223 pass in 240s. Previous commit 3a5cfc74 at 02:44 passed its run, so this may be transient (VTEncoderXPCService/aned state). Also: `timeout` is not on this Mac, so a bounded run needs a poll loop.
acceptance: The cause is named: the machine's media services, the number of these tests running at once, or something in the tests
Scripts/test.sh finishes on this Mac, or stops with a message naming the stuck test instead of sitting idle

CAUSE reproduced (pool starvation by text reads): VNRecognizeTextRequest hands part of each read to another thread at the caller's QoS and waits. From Swift's pool that is default QoS, and with every pool thread waiting in a read, nothing at default QoS runs at all (a plain DispatchQueue.global().async from a full pool never ran in 20s). Drills in the real runner (temp ZZPoolStarveDrillTests, deleted): 16 concurrent TextReader.words on the pool, nothing else running -> parked for good; 15 pool threads held + read on the last -> parked; same on a plain Thread -> parked; same on a .userInitiated queue -> 0.8s. 32 concurrent HEIF encodes on the pool -> 0.5s, so the HEIF/VCPHEVC and AVAssetReader parks were bystanders. Full Scripts/test.sh on HEAD before the fix parked at 0% CPU after ~3 min (sample: 10 threads TextReader.swift:763, 8 ImageCodec.swift:77).

FIX 35e19fb4: Sources/PhotonzRender/RecogniserLane.swift (userInitiated concurrent queue, width = cores/4, main thread inline) wraps the one Vision perform in TextReader.reading. Also protects the app: EditorState+RunWords reads rows in a task group. Scripts/test.sh: parked-run watch (180s quiet + <2s helper CPU -> sample, name tests, kill, exit 4; drill PHOTONZ_TEST_PARK_DRILL=1 PHOTONZ_TEST_QUIET_LIMIT=30 --filter ParkedRunDrill, verified stops in 84s naming aTestThatWaitsForNothing). TextReadsOnAFullPoolTests hangs on old code, 4.3s on new. Two full Scripts/test.sh runs green: 12716 in 306s, 12716 in 300s. Folded TitleSetFramesTests frame-time check passed in both full runs. Not re-tested straight after a batch of probe walks (my repro hung without walks, so walks were not the trigger). Left rough, no task: PlaytestLabelReader (probe-only) calls Vision directly; it runs on main so it is not exposed.

Cause named and reproduced: Vision text reads starve Swift's shared pool (16 reads at once park for good; on a userInitiated queue they answer). Fix in 35e19fb4: RecogniserLane routes every recognition off the pool, 4 at a time; Scripts/test.sh now stops a parked run after 3 quiet idle minutes, naming the tests (exit 4). Verified: new regression test red->green, two whole runs green (12,716 tests, 306s and 300s).
